memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "About three months later Judah was told, 'Your daughter-in-law Tamar is guilty of prostitution, and as a result she is now pregnant.' Judah said, 'Bring her out and have her burned to death!'" - Gen 38:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three months later, word reaches Judah that Tamar is pregnant — clearly, they assume, through immorality. And Judah's reaction is swift and severe: "Bring her out and have her burned to death!" He is instantly ready to condemn Tamar to a brutal punishment for the very kind of sin he himself had just committed with a "prostitute" by the roadside.

The hypocrisy is staggering. Judah thunders judgment against Tamar's supposed sexual sin while utterly ignoring his own. He has one standard for her and another for himself. He is quick, harsh, and merciless toward the sin of another — and completely blind to the plank in his own eye.

We should let this hold up a mirror to our own hearts. How often are we severe toward the failures of others while excusing our own? We can be outraged at someone else's sin that closely resembles our own, feeling righteous even as we condemn. This kind of hypocrisy is one of the things Jesus warned against most sharply (Matt 7:1-2).

The measure we use for others, Jesus said, will be measured to us. Before we rush to condemn, we would do well to remember our own need for mercy. Judah was about to be humbled by the very evidence he had handed over. Let us judge ourselves honestly before we judge others, and extend the grace we ourselves so desperately need.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I quick to condemn in others what I excuse in myself?
2. Where do I hold a harsher standard for others than for me?
3. How can I remember my own need for mercy before judging?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive my hypocrisy when I condemn in others what I excuse in myself. Help me to judge my own heart honestly first, and to extend the mercy I so deeply need. Amen.
